pop-causales.sinDatoDesc: No votes are recorded in the 'Total Votes' column of an election, in the boxes corresponding to the voting.
pop-causales.inconpletaDesc: Does not indicate the total number of citizens who voted, either in letters or numbers, or lacks one or two sections of the record.
pop-causales.errorMaterialDesc: With inconsistencies in the numerical data recorded.
pop-causales.ilegibilidadDesc: Contains signs, symbols, or characters other than: 0–9, Ø, (.), (-), (/), (\/), (=), -o-, or combinations of these, smudges, or amendments that make it impossible to identify the numbers.
pop-causales.sinFirmasDesc: The electoral record lacks the minimum number of polling station member signatures as required, or notes the absence of a member without proper replacement.
pop-causales.votosImpugnadosDesc: Electoral record containing one or more votes that were contested either during voting (identity issues) or counting (vote objection).
pop-causales.solicitudNulidadDesc: Record from a polling station where a nullity request was submitted by accredited representatives. The request is noted in any of the three sections.
pop-causales.actaExtravidaDesc: Polling station record that, due to reasons other than violence, was not delivered to the ODPE or entered into the electoral computing system.
pop-causales.actaSiniestradaDesc: Record not delivered due to violence or attacks affecting electoral materials.
pop-causales.obsrvacionesMultiplesDesc: Record that presents a combination of the previously mentioned observations.

PreguntasFrecuentes.R1: It is the process though which citizens elect the President of the Republic and two Vice Presidents. They serve for five (5) years, as established by the Political Constitution of Peru.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P2: What is the Senate election for single nationwide constituency (Distrito Electoral Único – DEU)?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R2A: This is the electoral process in which all voters within the national territory and Peruvians residing abroad constitute a single electoral district.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R2B: In this system, citizens vote for the same list of 30 candidates from across the country. In this way, senators are elected based on the votes obtained throughout the country.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R2C: The elected senators represent the country as a whole constituency, without specific territorial divisions.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P3: What is the Senate election for multi-member constituency (Distrito Electoral Múltiple – DEM)?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R3A: This is the electoral process though which citizens elect 30 senators to represent each electoral district in the country.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R3B: In this system, the national territory is divided into 27 electoral districts. These include country’s 24 regions, Lima Province, the Constitutional Province of Callao, and one district representing Peruvians residing abroad. Each electoral district elects one senator, except for Metropolitan Lima, which elects four.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R3C: This model ensures that all the regions of the country to have direct representation in the Senate.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P4: What is the Chamber of Deputies election?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R4A: This is the electoral process by which citizens elect 130 representatives to the Chamber of Deputies.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R4B: The election of deputies is carried out through multiple electoral districts. There are 27 electoral districts, comprised of the country’s 24 departments, plus Lima Province, the Constitutional Province of Callao, and one district corresponding to Peruvians residing abroad. Each district elects a specific number of deputies.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P5: What is the Andean Parliament election?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R5: It is the electoral process that allows citizens to elect the 5 Peruvian representatives to the Andean Parliament, a deliberative body of the Andean Integration System that promotes coordination and regional integration among member countries: Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, and Peru.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R6A: This is an optional mechanism that citizens can use to influence the selection of specific candidates from the list presented by a political organization.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R6B: For the election of national senators, deputies, and Andean Parliament representatives, voters can cast up to two preferential votes, while for regional senators, they may only cast one.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R6C: To use this mechanism, voters must write the number of their preferred candidate in the blank boxes located next to the symbol of the chosen political organization.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P7: What does voter turnout mean within the system?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R7: It is the percentage of voters who cast their vote compared to the total number of people eligible to vote.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P8: Where can I see voter turnout for my region?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R8: You can check it in the “Voter turnout” module.  There you will find a heat map and tables with detailed information by department, province, and district.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P9: Who announces the final election results?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R9A: The Jurado Nacional de Elecciones – JNE (National Elections Board) is responsible for proclaiming the final results.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R9B: The JNE reviews the challenged ballots, resolve appeals and challenges, and issues the official proclamation documents that establish the final results of the electoral process.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P10: How can I check the results from Peru and abroad?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R10: The results for Peru can be viewed at the national, regional, provincial, and district levels. For Peruvians residing abroad, results are available by continent, country, and city.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P11: How often are the results updated?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R11: The information is automatically updated as new records are received and processed. Each update shows the date and time of the last data processing cutoff.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P12: How do I know if the data is authentic?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R12: The information comes directly from the official ONPE database, using security and verification protocols that guarantee its integrity.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P13: Why do some tally sheets appear with observations?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R13: Because they contain incidents or inconsistencies that require review, so they are forwarded to the corresponding Jurado Electoral Especial – JEE (Special Electoral Jury) for evaluation, in accordance with current electoral regulations.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R14: It is an alternative mechanism equivalent to voting with a physical ballot, carried out through digital means.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P15: Can I search by polling station number or DNI number?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R15: Yes. In the “Advanced Queries” module, you can enter the polling station number or the DNI number to view the associated results.
PreguntasFrecuentes.R16: Yes. You can download the results in compressed .csv (.zip) formats, depending on the type of election or the geographic area selected.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P17: If I don't remember my polling station number, can I check using only my DNI number?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R17: Yes. The system allows you to check using only your ID number, as long as that the polling station associated with that DNI has already been processed.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P18: Can I use the system from a cell phone?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R18: Yes. The system is compatible with mobile devices and can be used on cell phones, tablets, and computers.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P19: Can I use the system if I don’t have an internet connection?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R19: No. The system requires an internet connection to load and update election results.
PreguntasFrecuentes.P20: Who can I contact if I want to submit a suggestion about the system?
PreguntasFrecuentes.R20: Suggestions can be submitted through the ONPE Help Desk, via email: soporte@onpe.gob.pe
